title: AtlasPay - legal / vendor approval / SLA & pricing sync
summary: Kickoff of vendor onboarding checklist focused on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets for token latency and availability, pricing approval path for a pilot, and KMS/HSM / data residency clarifications. Agreed to exchange redlined MSA, security package, and a finalized SLA spreadsheet; set a pilot pricing proposal and legal review timeline.
action_items: Priya Nair (SE) - produce SLA matrix with p50/p90/p99 token latency by model and region - due 2025-03-07
Alex Kim (AE) - send draft pilot pricing sheet and sample SOW - due 2025-03-06
Sam Carter (CSM) - share onboarding checklist and customer portal invite - due 2025-03-05
Maya Singh (Customer Legal) - return redlines on MSA/DPA or confirm major objections - due 2025-03-11
next_steps: Redwood to email redlined MSA template and security pack link
Redwood SE to run quick latency runbook and attach sample logs for audit
AtlasPay legal to consolidate redlines and schedule follow-up on 2025-03-11
Schedule pilot kickoff call after MSA/DPA are in review
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-04 15:00 PST | Duration: 52 minutes | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sam Carter (Redwood CSM), Jared Collins (AtlasPay VP Procurement), Maya Singh (AtlasPay Legal), Owen Park (AtlasPay CTO), Rita Huang (AtlasPay Security)

[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. Quick agenda — legal/msa, sla/pricing for pilot, and security questions. If we can get through that we should have clear owners.
[00:19] Jared Collins: Yep, thanks Alex. We're on a pretty compressed vendor approval timeline, legal wants the MSA and DPA back next week if possible. So, I guess first question — any standard enterprise MSA we can use as a starting point?
[00:29] Priya Nair: Yeah we have a standard enterprise MSA, i'll share the redlineable PDF. It's usually called Redwood Master Service Agreement v2.0. I will note there are a couple of enterprise clauses we see redlined often — data residency, indemnity ceilings, and audit rights.
[00:45] Maya Singh: For AtlasPay, indemnity and data residency stick. Also need to confirm breach notification timing — our security ops requires 48 hour notice for critical incidents. Is that feasible?
[00:55] Sam Carter: We can commit to 48 hours for confirmed incidents; for suspected incidents we usually do initial notification within 24 hours and confirm within 48. We'll put the precise language in the security pack.
[01:10] Owen Park: On DPA scope — we process PII for payments, so we need to ensure subprocessor list and any third-party infra is disclosed. Do you host outside US for the hosted model?
[01:21] Priya Nair: Hosted lives in multiple regions; we can region-lock requests to US or EU depending on account. For private / VPC deployments, customers run inside their VPC. We'll include a short note on subprocessor list and cloud regions.
[01:35] Rita Huang: KMS question: we require customer-managed keys. Does Redwood support KMS/HSM integrations?
[01:42] Alex Kim: Yes, we support customer KMS in Private deployments and in Dedicated via bring-your-own-key integrations with our enterprise package. For hosted we'll need to review the encryption at rest model — I'll have security attach the specifics.
[01:55] Jared Collins: Great. On SLA, legal and procurement want availability and latency numbers. Can you give p99 latency guarantees?
[02:05] Priya Nair: We usually offer availability SLAs for Dedicated contracts; hosted has best-effort unless it's in a reserved capacity plan. As for latency, we publish benchmark profiles — but formal p99 guarantees depend on dedicated capacity and the model shape. For a pilot we can propose target SLOs rather than hard SLA.
[02:24] Maya Singh: Procurement is okay with pilot SLOs if there's a rollback/fallback clause. Also need credits for outages during pilot.
[02:34] Alex Kim: That's reasonable. Typical approach is to include an SLA table for Dedicated with credits and have pilot terms include a credit schedule — we'll draft a pilot pricing + credit clause.
[02:44] [00:02:45] Jared Collins: Pricing — our finance wants a predictable cost model for the 90 day pilot. Do you do flat commit or usage-based?
[02:55] Alex Kim: We support both. For pilots we often do a blended model: a small committed monthly amount to reserve Dedicated capacity or named throughput, with overage at discounted usage rates. For hosted we do pure usage. I'll send a sample pilot pricing sheet.
[03:13] Owen Park: If we choose Dedicated, how quickly can you provision GPUs in our desired region and what's the lead time?
[03:22] Priya Nair: Provisioning Dedicated pools is typically 2-4 weeks depending on exact GPU type and quota; for quick pilots we sometimes use hosted dedicated burst capacity to get started in under a week. We'll note the region/instance constraints in the SOW.
[03:36] Maya Singh: On compliance artifacts, can you share SOC2 reports and penetration test summaries? Also, do you allow onsite audits?
[03:47] Sam Carter: Yes, SOC2 Type II is available under NDA; we have a summary pen-test report and can do virtual audits. Onsite audits are handled case-by-case; remote review usually suffices for initial procurement.
[03:58] Rita Huang: Do you have a record of third-party subprocessors? Need to know if any model hosting is on third-party managed services.
[04:05] Priya Nair: We'll attach the subprocessor matrix; for hosted many of the infra pieces are cloud providers but Redwood controls the runtime. For Private we don't use external infra.
[04:20] Alex Kim: To reduce back-and-forth, we'll send the MSA + DPA and a mapping doc: columns with clause, proposed Redwood language, and a rationale. That tends to speed legal reviews.
[04:33] Jared Collins: Perfect. Can we also get a named point of contact for security and contracts? Legal prefers a specific owner.
[04:40] Alex Kim: Sam Carter is the CSM and main contracts liaison; Priya will be SE for technical clarifications; I'm the AE running procurement. I'll include emails.
[04:51] [00:05:00] Maya Singh: A few redline specifics: 1) Limitation of liability — we need to understand caps tied to fees, 2) Data deletion timelines on contract termination, 3) Subprocessor notice and opt-out.
[05:04] Priya Nair: For data deletion we typically offer configurable retention in the console plus an immediate data purge API for private deployments. Hosted customers can request a certified deletion. We'll put standard deletion SLA: 30 days for hosted, immediate for private.
[05:22] Owen Park: Can you give a concrete example: if we do 100k tokens/day, what would latency look like for a 8k context model?
[05:33] Priya Nair: Roughly — depends on model family, quantization, and batch config. For a 8k context LLM on Dedicated with continuous batching, p50 ~40-80ms per token, p90 ~120-220ms, p99 can spike during GC or KV cache misses. I'll include real numbers in the SLA matrix.
[05:56] Jared Collins: That p99 range is wide; legal wants assurances. Will you commit to a max p99 for the pilot?
[06:04] Priya Nair: We can commit to a pilot target p99 with a mitigation clause — e.g., if p99 exceeds target for X days, we increase capacity or throttle non-critical workloads. It becomes operational detail in the SOW.
[06:20] Sam Carter: Operationally we can set up early monitoring alerts and an escalation path to Redwood on-call. We'll log incidents and share post-mortems.
[06:31] Rita Huang: Any limitations around logs and PII in logs? We need assurances logs won't contain full PII.
[06:40] Priya Nair: We can configure redaction and sampling; by default request/response logging is optional and can be disabled or scrubbed. We'll include the logging controls in the security pack.
[06:53] [00:07:00] Jared Collins: On signatures, is e-signature via DocuSign acceptable? Our legal requires DocuSign with audit trail.
[07:00] Alex Kim: Yes, DocuSign is fine. We use it for enterprise contracts.
[07:06] Maya Singh: Can we discuss DPA specifics: data controller vs processor language, subprocessors list, data retention schedules?
[07:15] Priya Nair: Redwood will be a processor; the DPA will specify subprocessors and retention. For retention we'll propose configurable policies with default 90 days for hosted logs and customer-configured TTL for persist stores.
[07:27] Owen Park: One more infra note — for private deployment, how much engineering involvement is expected from AtlasPay? Is there a managed option?
[07:36] Priya Nair: Private deployments come in tiers: self-hosted (customer-run), managed private (Redwood operates in your VPC), and on-prem appliance. Managed private includes Redwood ops support for provisioning and updates. We'll include deployment options in the SOW.
[07:51] Jared Collins: Ok finance sign-offs — we need to calculate run-rate cost for production if pilot scales. Where can we get a cost model?
[07:58] Alex Kim: We'll send a cost calc sheet that shows per-token costs, model perf multiplier, and Dedicated committed seat pricing. We'll run an initial projection for your 90-day pilot numbers.
[08:11] Maya Singh: Are there any legal terms that are absolute no-go? For example, indemnification tied to customer downstream liability?
[08:20] Alex Kim: We avoid open-ended indemnities; we typically cap indemnity to a multiple of fees and carve out certain liabilities. We'll mark those in the MSA for negotiation.
[08:31] [00:09:00] Jared Collins: What about export control / restricted model outputs? Any controls for generating regulated content?
[08:40] Priya Nair: Our content policy controls and optional prompt filtering can prevent known restricted categories. For payment data we recommend prompt engineering to avoid sending full raw card data to the model and use structured fields.
[08:55] Rita Huang: For audit logs, can we get sustained retention for forensic purposes beyond the 90-day default?
[09:02] Sam Carter: Yes, extended log retention is an add-on. We'll include pricing and options.
[09:10] Alex Kim: All right let's agree on tangible deliverables today — we will: 1) send MSA + DPA PDF with editable redlines, 2) attach security pack (SOC2, subprocessors, pen-test summary), 3) draft pilot SOW and pricing, 4) SE to provide SLA matrix and latency samples.
[09:28] Jared Collins: That covers it. Is there an escalation path if legal and procurement disagree on payment security terms?
[09:36] Alex Kim: Yes, we have an escalation to the partnerships and legal team. If needed we'll schedule a session between your counsel and our GC.
[09:44] Maya Singh: Can we put an action for Redwood to flag any non-standard MSA clauses up front so we don't do cyclical redlines?
[09:51] Alex Kim: Absolutely, we'll annotate the MSA with callouts and rationale.
[09:58] [00:10:00] Priya Nair: Small technical note — when we say p99 latency guarantees, the measurement semantics matter. We use request-level latency measured at the service ingress including network hops within the region. We'll include the metric definitions in the SLA matrix.
[10:14] Owen Park: Also note concurrency patterns — spikes in concurrent sessions can elevate p99, so capacity planning will be driven by concurrency and token throughput.
[10:25] Priya Nair: Right, we'll show sample charts mapping concurrency to observed p99 at different models.
[10:33] Jared Collins: For the pilot, what model family do you recommend for AtlasPay given we need structured outputs and deterministic responses?
[10:41] Priya Nair: For structured output and lower hallucinations, we often recommend instruction-tuned LLMs with higher quality—if cost is a concern we can look at mid-tier open models with quantization. We'll recommend two model families in the pilot pricing sheet.
[10:58] Maya Singh: One last legal Q — data subject requests handling. Do you assist in DSARs?
[11:05] Alex Kim: We assist with logs and data exports for DSARs; the process is in the DPA. We'll provide a DSAR playbook.
[11:15] Sam Carter: Okay, quick recaps and owners: MSA/DPA will be sent by Alex; Priya will attach latency/SLA docs; Sam will send onboarding steps and portal invites.
[11:28] Jared Collins: Timeline — assuming Redlines come back in a week, procurement wants signature before end of month. Is that realistic?
[11:37] Alex Kim: It's tight but possible. If legal returns redlines by 2025-03-11 we can iterate and target signature by 2025-03-28 assuming no major blockers.
[11:49] Maya Singh: We'll try to consolidate our redlines and call out must-haves vs nice-to-haves to speed up negotiation.
[11:58] Rita Huang: Any examples of prior customers with similar compliance needs we can reference?
[12:05] Sam Carter: We can provide a short case note (anonymized) for a financial services customer that did a Private deployment with KMS. I'll attach that.
[12:15] [00:13:00] Alex Kim: OK, last question — any competitors you want us to call out for feature/perf comparisons?
[12:22] Jared Collins: Our team looked at Anthropic and AWS Bedrock; they want perf numbers vs Redwood for same model families.
[12:31] Priya Nair: We'll include benchmark comparisons where available; note that model variants and quantization make direct apples-to-apples tricky but we'll provide guided comparisons.
[12:44] Maya Singh: Thanks, that helps.
[12:49] Alex Kim: All right if there are no more questions let's wrap and I'll follow up with the materials within 48 hours.
[12:57] Jared Collins: That's great, appreciate it.
[13:02] Owen Park: Thanks all.
[13:05] Sam Carter: Closing meeting — next sync target 2025-03-11 for legal redline review.

Notes: Links shared in chat: MSA draft (https://redwood.example.com/shared/MSA/Redwood_MSA_v2_editable.pdf), Security pack (https://redwood.example.com/security/atlaspay_security_pack.zip), Pilot pricing template (https://redwood.example.com/sales/pilot_pricing_template.xlsx)

End of transcript.
